subject: Maintenance rollback window & service-credit mediation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@stellarnet.com>; Procurement <procurement@stellarnet.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Maintenance rollback window & service-credit mediation

Hi Priya / StellaNet team —

Thanks for sharing your order-form comments yesterday. We pulled together a short counterproposal focused on three items you flagged: maintenance rollback timing, the per-outage service-credit cap, and P1 response SLA. Attached: Redwood_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx (highlights in comments).

Quick summary of our positions:
- Maintenance rollback: propose a 60-minute rollback window for routine rolling upgrades; for emergency rollbacks we can commit to a 30-minute start-to-initiate target (noting variability with large KV-state migrations).
- Service-credit cap: we propose a monthly cap of 25% of monthly recurring charges (MRC) for systemic outages, with an exception path for repeated SLA misses tied to remediation plans.
- P1 response: 15-minute acknowledgement with a 2-hour initial mitigation/update for on-call during business hours; 4-hour mitigation target outside core hours.

Action items: can your legal/procurement team confirm whether the 25% cap is an acceptable starting point? Also, Priya, could you share any internal blackout dates (global maintenance freeze) that would change our rollout plan?

I copied Lauren and Kim to loop in legal and ops feasibility. Marcus — can you confirm the rollback timing is operationally achievable across our multi-region pools?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0137

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx (comments), Redwood_Maintenance_Runbook.pdf

From: Priya Singh <priya@stellarnet.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@stellarnet.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Maintenance rollback window & service-credit mediation

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear summary and the annotated doc. Two quick clarifications from procurement/legal:
1) The 25% monthly cap is higher than our standard appetite for mission-critical infra — would Redwood consider a stepped cap (10% first quarter, 15% second, 25% thereafter) tied to adoption and operational history?
2) On rollbacks: our concern is a rollback triggering data inconsistency across regions; we need a clearer escalation and verification protocol before rollback completion.

I'm attaching StellaNet_SLA_asks.xlsx with our scoring and suggested language. Procurement would like your legal counsel to sync with our counsel (CloudTrust Legal) to iron out wording around repeat outages and remediation obligations.

Also, our Ops team has a global blackout window for product launches: May 20 – May 23. That will constrain any planned rolling upgrades.

Thanks —
Priya Singh
Head of Procurement, StellaNet
priya@stellarnet.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@stellarnet.com>; CloudTrust Legal <legal@cloudtrust.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Maintenance rollback window & service-credit mediation

Thanks, Jonas. Looping Legal and Ops into a focused path forward. A few legal notes on our side:
- Stepped cap: acceptable as a commercial concession if we include explicit triggers for acceleration (e.g., two separate monthly SLA shortfalls triggers cap move). We should limit the lookback window to 90 days for triggers.
- Repeat outages: we'll propose a remediation plan clause with milestones and a right to terminate if remediation milestones are missed for 3 consecutive months.
- Blackout window: we can carve out the May 20–23 dates from planned rollouts, but need to preserve emergency maintenance rights for security hotfixes — propose a 24-hour notice for emergency security fixes during blackouts, plus post-facto incident report.

Marcus / Kim — operational feasibility checks: 60-minute rollback for routine rolling upgrades vs 30-minute emergency initiation — can you confirm the assumptions (avg partition size, KV resync window) in the runbook align? If not, propose alternative timeboxes.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Maintenance rollback window & service-credit mediation

Quick ops check: we reviewed the runbook and ran a dry-run on a staging cluster that mirrors StellaNet's approximate traffic profile. Findings:
- Routine rolling upgrade rollback to previous binary + schema-safe migration: median start-to-initiate ~42 minutes, 95th percentile ~75 minutes. So a 60-minute target is reasonable as a SLA for routine rolling upgrades with the caveat we exclude very large KV-store reseeds (>2TB) from the 60-minute guarantee.
- Emergency rollback initiation (stop + revert switch): achievable to start within 20–30 minutes; full service recovery depends on background resync and can span several hours in extreme cases.
- We can add a verification protocol: checksum validation step and cross-region reconciliation before declaring rollback complete; that adds ~15–45 minutes depending on dataset.

Proposal for contract language: keep 60-minute rollback SLA for routine upgrades, emergency initiation target at 30 minutes, and an explicit exclusion for very large state migrations with an example threshold (>2TB). We'll surface the detailed numbers in the runbook appendix.

Kim / Lauren — happy to prep the appendix and put numbers next to the runbook sections for clarity.

Marcus
VP, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2029 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Maintenance rollback window & service-credit mediation

Hi all —

We reviewed Redwood's proposed language and StellaNet's asks. CloudTrust can coordinate a redline exchange tomorrow morning (we're EST-based). A couple of drafting points we recommend to reduce ambiguity:
- Define "initiate" vs "complete" for rollback events (we suggest: initiate = rollback command issued and failover begun; complete = validation checks passed and all nodes report healthy).
- For stepped caps, include an explicit measurement cadence (monthly measurement with 30-day cure rights) and preserve a carveout for security incidents that cause credits to not apply.
- On termination/remediation: instead of an immediate right to terminate after three missed milestones, add an opportunity for a formal remediation plan meeting and a 45-day cure period; only then allow termination if remediation fails.

We will prepare a marked-up order form and share a DocuSign packet once commercial language is agreed.

Regards,
A. Mendoza
Senior Counsel, CloudTrust Legal
legal@cloudtrust.com
